profiles.title: The Entrance of the Mother of God into the Temple
profiles.subject: Feasts

overview.text: The Entrance concerns Mary as a child entering the Jerusalem Temple. Hopko’s OCA explanation gives November 21 and identifies the narrative as Church tradition without direct biblical or historical documentation. It should be distinguished from the February feast of Christ’s Presentation.

blocks.text: The young Mary approaches Zacharias, with Joachim and Anna behind her. Maidens carry candles; an additional scene may depict her receiving food from an angel.

blocks.text: The traditional account describes her parents bringing Mary to be raised in service to God, her welcome by Zacharias, and her nourishment by angels. Hopko identifies the child’s entry as preparing the living sanctuary of the divine Child. His explanation draws attention to the liturgical use of Old Testament temple passages and Mary’s Magnificat, rather than treating the story as a passage omitted from the canonical Gospels.

blocks.text: The published meaning centers on Mary herself becoming the dwelling place of God. Hopko relates this to the New Testament description of God dwelling with human beings and the Church as a spiritual house. The imagery connects the Temple with the Incarnation; it is not an instruction for reenacting the child’s entry.

images.title: Russian - Presentation of the Virgin in the Temple - Walters 372410.jpg
images.description: This scene is rarely met with as a separate icon, although it occurs as one of the subjects on smaller ones. The subject is one of the church's Twelve Festivals, which were represented on the third tier of the iconostasis (alter screen and icon stand combined), which divided the sanctuary from the nave. It depicts the Virgin's presentation in the Temple. In accordance with traditional iconography used for representing this holy fest, the Virgin, the smaller figure in the foreground, is being presented by her parents Joachim and Anna to the priest Zacharias, who holds out hands to bless her. The seven taper-bearing daughters of Zion (daughters of Israel), friends of the Virgin, stand behind Joachim and Anna. The large dimensions of this panel demonstrate the great size to which an iconostasis could attain.
